sample_data.method: bundled file + file upload + paste JSON
sample_data.reset_instructions: Press the header Reset button (or Verify & Data → Reset to published data) to restore the bundled published fixture and discard imported batches; reloading the page has the same effect because all state is in-memory.

problem_solving_method: We encoded every ruling from CLARIFICATIONS.md (R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-29) as isolated pure functions in a deterministic TypeScript engine, built a fail-soft adapter that validates and normalises the official case format (subjects/compulsory/students) without crashing on bad rows, and wrapped it in a trace-first UI: every displayed GPA can be expanded into a step-by-step walkthrough that cites the ruling and the student's real numbers. Because determinism is the problem's defining property, we added a proof layer: a canonical serialisation of the normalised input and every output row is hashed with a self-contained, NIST-vector-verified SHA-256 — the Proof tab re-runs the whole pipeline three times live (byte-identical hashes), and one command (bun scripts/fingerprint.ts PUB-02) reproduces the identical fingerprint from the repository source. The published fixture (25 cases, 1,765 students) ships bundled, judges' hidden cases in the same shape load through the same upload/paste pipeline, and a 114-assertion suite (CLI + in-browser) re-derives the GPA formula for every published student and asserts byte-identical determinism.

team_members.major_contribution: Entire solution: rule engine, fixture adapter, verification suite, UI views, documentation and deployment.

major_design_decisions: Official case format as the app's native input: bundled fixture, file upload and pasted JSON all pass through one validated adapter, so hidden judge cases in the same shape are just another batch.
Pure deterministic engine with no randomness, dates or network in the calculation path; identical input produces byte-identical export JSON (asserted in the suite).

Determinism turned into evidence: canonical input/output serialisation + SHA-256 fingerprint (self-contained implementation, asserted against NIST test vectors). The Proof tab recomputes ×3 live and scripts/fingerprint.ts reproduces the identical hash from source, so the deployed app and the shipped code are verifiably the same machine; any single-mark change alters the fingerprint (tamper seal).
Judge Console (⌘K command palette): judges audit anything in seconds — roll, name, rule id, letter, batch switch, exports, self-test — without clicking through tabs.

Fail-soft validation: malformed marks never crash a batch — each issue is reported with student/subject scope and the student is still processed deterministically (missing compulsory marks become AB).
Trace-first UI: the trace cites the ruling id (R-11/R-12/R-13) together with the student's actual numbers so every GPA is auditable without reading code.

Ten hand-crafted hard-edge students (rolls 101–106 and 201–204 in batch DEMO-EDGE-10) cover every boundary the rules define; each trace carries a 'why this student matters' note with a hand-derivation a judge can follow, presented as deep-linkable Edge Case Files.
Non-practical subjects use the standard 33/100 pass mark implied by the published grade scale (R-11 defines part pass marks only for split subjects); documented in README Known limitations.
known_limitations: Full-subject (non-practical) pass mark assumed 33/100 from the standard scale; a hidden case expecting a different value would need the one-line constant changed in engine.ts.
GPA divisor fixed at 6 per R-13 regardless of a case's compulsory-subject count (published cases always list six).
Practical-fail list counts only subjects the student sat; AB in a practical subject places the student on the absent list instead.
Exports cover the current batch only; no multi-batch combined export.
